overview: Mercia was a kingdom in central England. Large earthworks and the Staffordshire Hoard offer different views of its region: organized construction and highly skilled early medieval metalwork.

items.text: Offa's Dyke used a bank and ditch to mark a frontier. English Heritage dates its construction probably to the 780s.
Staffordshire Hoard fragments include intricate gold and garnet decoration. Their designs have connections across several European regions.
Many hoard fragments belonged to an elaborate helmet. Modern reconstruction relies on study of the surviving pieces rather than discovery of an intact helmet.
The hoard reveals elite craftsmanship and equipment. Its burial location alone cannot identify every maker or make it a representative sample of ordinary Mercian households.
Scholars from Mercia contributed to the translations supported by Alfred of Wessex. Learned activity crossed the boundaries between neighboring kingdoms.

sources.title: English Heritage: History of Offas Dyke
